label: Static Site Generators
description: Properties built with static site generators — Hugo, Jekyll, 11ty, Astro (static mode) — where all pages are pre-rendered at build time with no server-side runtime. These properties represent the purest form of content-driven SEO: no JavaScript rendering concerns, no server-side logic, no dynamic content complications. E.V.O. learns the baseline of what organic performance looks like when stripped of all technical confounders — making this cohort's intelligence invaluable as a control group for diagnosing technical issues in other cohorts.

defining_seo_characteristics.primary_content_type: Documentation, blog posts, landing pages, portfolio pages, knowledge base articles
defining_seo_characteristics.typical_conversion_path: Blog post / doc page → product landing page → external signup or contact
key_seo_challenges: Build time scaling — large content corpora can create slow build pipelines that delay publishing
No dynamic content — personalization, A/B testing, and dynamic features require client-side JavaScript that may affect CWV
Limited interactivity without JavaScript islands — search, filtering, and forms require additional architecture
Content freshness perception — static sites may signal lower crawl priority to Google if rebuild frequency is low
No server-side redirects without hosting platform support — redirect management depends on deployment platform (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages)
key_seo_opportunities: Perfect Core Web Vitals scores — pre-rendered HTML with minimal JavaScript delivers the fastest possible page loads
Zero JavaScript rendering risk — Googlebot receives the same HTML as users, eliminating all rendering-based indexation issues
Simple, flat URL structures that are inherently crawl-efficient
Markdown-based content workflows that integrate naturally with developer tooling and version control
CDN-first hosting (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages) providing global edge delivery with zero server management

fleet_intelligence_notes.cross_industry_transfer: Very high. Static site SEO patterns are almost entirely content-driven — the architecture contributes virtually zero technical variance. This makes the cohort's intelligence transferable as a content-quality baseline across all other cohorts. When E.V.O. sees a technically complex site underperforming, comparing it against the static site baseline reveals how much of the underperformance is architectural vs. content-driven.
fleet_intelligence_notes.protocol_sequencing_pattern: Typically: Content Opportunity → Link Architecture → Meta Surgeon → Index Diagnostic. Static sites rarely have indexation issues. The bottleneck is almost always content strategy and authority building. Index Diagnostic comes last as a validation step, not a primary intervention.

industries.label: Developer Documentation
industries.description: Technical documentation sites for software tools, libraries, and frameworks. The static site generator is the canonical platform for developer docs — fast, version-controllable, and markdown-native.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and navigational — developers looking up specific API methods, configurations, and implementation patterns
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — documentation sites compete primarily with their own project's GitHub README and Stack Overflow answers

industries.label: Personal Brands / Thought Leadership
industries.description: Individual expert and thought leader websites. Blog content establishes authority in a domain. The personal brand IS the content strategy — every post builds the individual's organic reputation.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — readers seeking expert perspectives on specific topics
high_value_content_types: deep-dive technical or industry blog posts
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — personal brand queries are uncontested. Topical authority queries face competition from larger publications

industries.label: Small Agency / Studio Sites
industries.description: Boutique agency and design studio websites. Portfolio-focused with minimal content velocity. SEO value comes from niche expertise content and local/service-area targeting.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation — potential clients evaluating small agencies for specific projects
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low-moderate — small agencies compete locally and within niche specializations

industries.label: Technical Blogging / Content
industries.description: Technical blog sites focused on programming, engineering, or technology topics. Content depth and originality are the primary ranking signals — static generators are the preferred platform for technical writers.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — developers and engineers seeking solutions to specific technical problems
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — competing against Stack Overflow, Medium, and dev.to for technical query visibility

industries.label: Indie SaaS / Solo Founders
industries.description: Marketing sites for indie SaaS products built by solo founders or small teams. Static generators are the pragmatic choice — fast to build, zero server costs, low maintenance.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation — potential users evaluating the product against alternatives
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Varies by niche — indie SaaS competes against funded competitors with larger content teams. Long-tail niche targeting is the primary strategy

industries.label: Podcast / Newsletter Brands
industries.description: Companion websites for podcasts and newsletters. Static sites serve as the SEO surface for audio/email content that Google can't directly index — show notes and archives create the organic footprint.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and navigational — listeners/readers finding specific episodes or discovering the show through topic searches
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — podcast companion sites face minimal organic competition for episode-specific and guest-specific queries

industries.label: Event / Conference Sites
industries.description: Websites for conferences, meetups, and events. Static generators handle the annual rebuild cycle well — new content for each event iteration built on top of the previous year's archival content.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Navigational and informational — attendees seeking event details and potential attendees evaluating the event
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Very low — event-specific queries are uncontested. Broader conference category queries face moderate competition

industries.label: Research / Academic Projects
industries.description: Research project websites, academic paper companion sites, and scholarly content hubs. Static sites preserve research outputs as permanent, citable web resources.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — researchers and students seeking specific studies, datasets, and methodologies
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — academic content competes primarily with Google Scholar, ResearchGate, and institutional .edu sites

industries.label: Small Nonprofit / Community
industries.description: Small nonprofits and community organizations using static sites for low-maintenance, low-cost web presence. SEO is often the primary discovery channel given zero advertising budget.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and navigational — community members seeking services and information
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Very low — small nonprofits compete locally for cause-specific queries with minimal competition

industries.label: Photography / Visual Portfolio
industries.description: Photographer and visual artist portfolio sites. Unique SEO challenge — image-heavy sites with minimal text content. Image SEO (alt text, file naming, schema) is the primary optimization surface.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Navigational and commercial — potential clients seeking photographers in a specific style or location
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — photographer portfolio sites compete locally and within style niches

industries.label: Local Tech Business
industries.description: Small local technology businesses (IT services, web development, tech repair) using static sites. Local SEO with a modern technical foundation — demonstrating capability through the site itself.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Local and commercial — businesses and individuals seeking nearby tech services
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate locally — IT services and web development queries are competitive in metro areas, less so in smaller markets

industries.label: Product Landing Pages
industries.description: Standalone product launch and marketing landing pages. Static generators provide fast, reliable single-page or few-page sites optimized for a specific product launch or campaign.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation and navigational — users evaluating a specific product
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Varies — depends entirely on the product category. The site itself has minimal organic footprint to build authority

industries.label: Internal / Company Knowledge Bases
industries.description: Public-facing company knowledge bases and help centers built on static generators. FAQ content, troubleshooting guides, and product documentation that serves both customers and search engines.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — customers seeking answers to specific product questions and troubleshooting steps
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — knowledge base queries are typically brand-specific with minimal external competition
